name: Drift
use_label: Video editing for Shorts and game clips
one_liner: Multi-track video editor for Shorts and game clips, with no subscription or watermark

text.why: Built on Qt 6 and FFmpeg, it puts a multi-track timeline (trim, split, snap, ripple), GPU effects and transitions, auto captions you can edit line by line, click-to-cut-out subjects, masks, green screen and multicam in one window. A built-in local MCP server (off by default) lets Cursor or Claude Code place clips and export from the open project. It ships on Flathub, Windows, macOS (Apple Silicon) and as Android APKs; the latest release is v0.6.0 (2026-09-13).
text.take: A GPLv3 editor that flatly refuses the usual ending of a free editor — a watermark or a login wall — with the caveat that it is still in 0.x releases.
build: Because the MCP server lets an agent import media, place clips and export, you could wire up a semi-automatic pipeline that cuts one long recording into several Shorts. GPL-3.0 means derivatives must publish their source.

who.situation: generate captions, then fix each line
MP4 and GIF export without a watermark

who.role: Developers automating edits with an AI agent
who.situation: local MCP server, off until enabled

start.text: # Windows (.exe / portable zip), macOS (.dmg, Apple Silicon) and Android (APK) builds are on the latest GitHub release
adb install Drift-*-arm64-v8a.apk   # on a phone

caveat: GPL-3.0 — modified or redistributed builds must publish source
macOS build is Apple Silicon only; Android is a sideloaded APK, not on the Play Store
Latest release v0.6.0 (2026-09-13), still 0.x; fonts, stickers, extra effects and speech models download separately inside the Addon Manager

license.scope_text: Use freely. Release your source if you redistribute (copyleft).
